## The dashboard

::: {.notes}
The dashboard was rebuilt on 13 September on the corrected protocol, so that it says exactly what this talk says, simplified on 14 September for a reader with no statistics, and refreshed on 16 September with the 570-layer predictor set that has no DHS in it. Start here now opens with a plain-language abstract (the project, the four training surveys, how the model was built and checked), then the three numbers, one card on how to use the map, and the checklist; the Ghana worked example and the audit history sit in folded panels. Removed with the rebuild: the person-level machine-learning layer (a coin toss under honest folds), the earlier area-level estimators and their intervals, the old leaderboard, the GBD placeholder and the Sierra Leone chiefdom layer. One estimator feeds every tab: the index fitted on all surveyed districts of a country and applied to every district. The chance of being in the worst fifth exists for surveyed districts in three countries; Sierra Leone's 14 districts cannot be cross-validated. A printable brief per country comes from the same tables, and a 25-page static walkthrough of every tab (dashboard_walkthrough_2026-09-14.pdf in the Dropbox folder) is there for written comments. Open items: sharing a view by URL, faster loading (the boundary files are most of the bundle), the worst-fifth probability for unsurveyed districts, and plain-language descriptions for the predictors (75 of 570 have one; the catalog is the worklist). Open the URL a few minutes before showing it: the free tier stops idle instances and the restart takes a minute.
:::

## The geostatistical model estimates levels better and ranks worse

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="34%"}
The DHS Program's model-based geostatistics fitted at the survey clusters (a spatial field plus covariates), scored on the same district folds. On the level it scores `r f2(Q$mbg_mbg)` against `r f2(Q$mbg_index)` for the index (index better in `r Q$mbg_index_better` of `r Q$mbg_cells` outcome-country combinations); on prevalence `r f2(Q$mbg_mbg_p)` against `r f2(Q$mbg_index_p)`.
:::
::: {.column width="66%"}
```{r geostat, fig.width=5.8, fig.height=4.6, dpi=160}
if (!is.null(MBG)) {
  lab <- c(domain_index = "Zero-tuning domain index", mbg = "Geostatistical, field + domain covariates", mbg_dhs = "Geostatistical, field + DHS covariate list", mbg_gp = "Geostatistical, field only", spatial = "Spatial smoother", region_mean_jk = "Jackknifed regional mean")
  d <- MBG |> filter(estimand %in% c("infill", "region"), arm %in% names(lab)) |> cell_ci("rho_agg", c("estimand", "target", "arm")) |>
    mutate(Model = factor(lab[arm], levels = rev(lab)), panel = paste(c(infill = "In-fill", region = "Region")[estimand], tlab[target], sep = ", "))
  forest(d, "Model", facet = "panel", null = 0, base = 12, xlab = "Spearman across districts (mean, 95% interval)")
}
```
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
INLA-SPDE Matern field with penalized-complexity priors, binomial on cluster counts for prevalence and Gaussian for the level, cluster predictions aggregated to districts by effective sample size; run with the first component of every covariate domain and with the DHS Program's ten-raster list (`r f2(Q$mbg_dhs)` on the level). The field alone scores `r f2(Q$mbg_gp)`. The geostatistical model has the lower absolute error on prevalence (`r f2(Q$mbg_w_mbg, 1)` against `r f2(Q$mbg_w_index, 1)` percentage points) because it estimates a level and shrinks toward it. Under region extrapolation the index scores `r f2(Q$mbg_region_index)` against `r f2(Q$mbg_region_mbg)`. The method needs measured clusters inside the country it predicts, so it has no country-transport estimand. Likely question: whether the two are complementary. Yes: the geostatistical model for a calibrated prevalence where a survey exists, the index for a ranking where none does.
:::

## Every column kept or dropped has a written reason

```{r pipeline}
kb(df(Step = c("Assemble", "Append blocks", "Exclude", "Stamp", "Fit-time policy", "Transport matrix"),
  `What happens` = c("Base extraction on the spine, food environment, extra sources, add-back sources", "Household budget surveys, MICS microdata, RTFP prices, MODIS NDVI, climate normals", "Rules with a written reason: data defects, superseded layers, redundant twins", "Access tier, within-country variation, alignment rule, year used and gap, modelled-surface flag", "Drop national constants and leakage columns", "Per country: coverage of at least 70% and some variation; then the four-country intersection"),
  Columns = c("", as.character(Q$n_assembled), as.character(Q$n), as.character(Q$n), as.character(Q$n_declared %||% 525), as.character(Q$n_common %||% 464))), digits = 0)
```

::: {.notes}
One shell script runs the chain (scripts/covariates/rebuild_shared_tail.sh) and ends in an audit that fails the build on a domain-key collision, a column declared subnational that does not vary, or a join that fans out. The exclusion file has `r if (!is.null(EX)) nrow(EX) else 22` rules and every rule states its evidence: a nitrogen layer whose medians differ thirtyfold between countries, an NDVI product declared available only to 2013, calendar-year series superseded by survey-year values. This week's most instructive mistake was in the exclusions. A review labeled the soil dispersion bands and the 20-50 cm depth means "redundant" on a mechanistic argument, and the climate-and-soil result fell from 0.37 to 0.34 across districts and from 0.45 to 0.40 across regions. The bands correlate only 0.03 to 0.69 with the depth means, so the label was wrong; restoring them brought both numbers back. We now hold to one rule: nothing is added or regrouped because a score likes it, an exclusion whose stated premise fails on its own metric is reverted, and every set change is checked against the transport arms before a run. What a model can see is the last two rows: `r Q$n_declared %||% 525` columns vary within a country, of which `r Q$n_common %||% 464` have a value in all four countries and so can be used to predict a new one. The rest are per-country data gaps: household budget diet indicators pending for Ghana and Sierra Leone, RTFP for The Gambia and Malawi only, MICS items absent from one round.
:::

## From columns to domains

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="34%"}
`r Q$n_dom` domains. A domain groups columns by what they measure, whatever the source: the MAP, IHME and survey malaria columns sit in one group. Each domain enters the model as its leading principal components, to 80% of variance and at most twelve, learned on the training districts only.
:::
::: {.column width="66%"}
```{r domains, fig.width=6.2, fig.height=5.6, dpi=160}
if (!is.null(MD)) {
  d <- as.data.frame(table(Domain = MD$domain, Tier = MD$tier_lab), stringsAsFactors = FALSE); d <- d[d$Freq > 0, ]
  tot <- tapply(d$Freq, d$Domain, sum); d$Domain <- factor(d$Domain, levels = names(sort(tot))); d$Tier <- factor(d$Tier, levels = names(tier_col))
  ggplot(d, aes(Freq, Domain, fill = Tier)) + geom_col(width = 0.72) +
    geom_text(data = df(Domain = factor(names(tot), levels = levels(d$Domain)), n = as.vector(tot)), aes(n, Domain, label = n), inherit.aes = FALSE, hjust = -0.2, size = 3.2) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = tier_col) + scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) + labs(x = "Columns", y = NULL, fill = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11) + theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom") + guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2))
}
```
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
Why domains: `r Q$n` columns against 14 to 87 districts per country cannot be fitted column by column, and the columns are heavily correlated within a source. Grouping them by what they measure and taking principal components inside each group keeps most of the variance of each group, treats a source with 64 columns and a source with 3 as one construct each, and keeps the outcome out of the representation: the rotations are learned from the training districts' predictors alone, so nothing is selected on the biomarker. The grouping is written down: each source block brings a label, and `r if (!is.null(OV)) nrow(OV) else 10` override rules in metadata/covariates/domain_overrides.csv regroup columns by construct (infection and inflammation burden, immunisation, anemia, child anthropometry, infant feeding, supplementation, water and sanitation, education, child mortality, assets), so that MAP, IHME, DHS and MICS versions of the same thing are weighed together. Two things went wrong this week and are now guarded. A domain's first twelve characters are its key inside the model; two labels that shared them ("Food prices (RTFP)" and "Food prices and supply") were silently merged in two analyzes until a check caught it on 16 September. The other is in the exclusions, on the next slide. One more point for questions: climate alone or soil alone transports better than all domains together, the analysis deck's climate-and-soil result.
:::

## The twenty layers behind child iron, and how much each carries

```{r twenty-iron, fig.width=11, fig.height=6.4, dpi=170}
if (!is.null(IT)) {
  d <- IT |> filter(outcome == "child_iron", target == "level", rank <= 20) |>
    mutate(name = ifelse(is.na(PLAIN[column]), clean_code(column), unname(PLAIN[column])),
           lab = sprintf("%.1f%%%s", 100 * share, ifelse(incountry_sign_agree == incountry_fits, "  *", "")), name = factor(name, levels = rev(name)))
  doms <- sort(unique(d$domain)); pal <- c("#1f4e79", "#6baed6", "#8c510a", "#33a02c", "#b15928", "#6a3d9a", "#e08214", "#0F7B8A", "#cab2d6", "#fdbf6f", "#d7191c", "#9e9ac8", "#7fcdbb", "#fdae61")
  ggplot(d, aes(beta_std, name, fill = domain)) + geom_col(width = 0.72) + geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey40") +
    geom_text(aes(label = lab, x = ifelse(beta_std > 0, beta_std + 0.1, beta_std - 0.1), hjust = ifelse(beta_std > 0, 0, 1)), size = 3.3, colour = "grey30") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = stats::setNames(rep(pal, length.out = length(doms)), doms)) + scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = 0.18)) +
    labs(x = "Standardised weight in the pooled index (left: district ranks better; right: worse)
Label: share of the index carried; * = same direction in each country's own fit", y = NULL, fill = NULL) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) + theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.text = element_text(size = 9), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), axis.title.x = element_text(size = 9.5)) + guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE))
}
```

::: {.notes}
index_importance_top.csv, child iron, biomarker level: the twenty largest standardized weights in the pooled four-country fit, drawn as bars so their sizes can be compared. The level target is the negated log ferritin, so a bar to the right means districts with more of the layer rank worse on child iron, to the left better. The label is the share of the index's variance the layer carries: the twenty together hold about a fifth of the index (`r if (!is.null(IT)) sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * sum(IT$share[IT$outcome == "child_iron" & IT$target == "level" & IT$rank <= 20])) else "21%"`), the rest is spread over the other 350 columns, which is how a weighted sum of many weak signals is meant to behave. All twenty keep their direction in every leave-one-country-out fit; the starred ones (`r if (!is.null(IT)) sum(IT$incountry_sign_agree[IT$outcome == "child_iron" & IT$target == "level" & IT$rank <= 20] == IT$incountry_fits[IT$outcome == "child_iron" & IT$target == "level" & IT$rank <= 20]) else 10` of twenty) also keep it in each country's own separate fit, the stricter test. The story is the one on the earlier slides: cereal-heavy cropping, ruminant and cattle density, cropland, distance from the coast and a high dependency ratio rank a district worse; root crops, higher plant productivity, relatively expensive staples, modeled overweight and malaria intensity rank it better, the last for the geographic reason discussed. None of the twenty requires a blood sample, and the twenty-layer equal-weight composite scores about the same as the full index for a new country.
:::

## Exclusions, with their reasons

```{r exclusions}
if (!is.null(EX)) {
  e <- EX |> transmute(Rule = canonical_regex, Policy = policy, Reason = ifelse(nchar(reason) > 110, paste0(substr(reason, 1, 107), "..."), reason))
  kb(e, digits = 0)
}
```

::: {.notes}
metadata/covariates/exclusions.csv, applied by scripts/protocol_v2/53_apply_exclusion_policy.R to the live set. Data defects are removed on evidence in the audit tables; superseded layers are replaced by a better-aligned version of the same quantity; redundant twins are removed when a pooled rank correlation reaches 0.98 with a kept column. The two soil rules that failed that standard were removed on 15 September (SX-01 in the sandbox log).
:::

## Predictor set by domain and tier

```{r domain-table}
if (!is.null(MD)) {
  t <- MD |> group_by(Domain = domain) |> summarise(Columns = n(), `Open` = sum(tier == "open"), `Public microdata` = sum(tier == "survey_public"), `DHS` = sum(tier == "survey_dhs"),
                                                    `Vary within country` = sum(subn), `Modelled surfaces` = sum(as.logical(toupper(as.character(modelled_surface))), na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |> arrange(desc(Columns))
  kb(t, digits = 0)
}
```

::: {.notes}
Modeled surfaces are estimates produced by someone else's model (IHME, MAP, the MIMI dietary inadequacy estimates); they are included by default and the protocol has a switch (V2_DROP_MODELLED=1) to score without them. Columns that do not vary within a country are the national constants dropped at fit time.
:::

## What we would add next, and the rule for adding it

- Sub-national household-survey microdata with GPS: MICS cluster coordinates for Ghana 2017-18 and Malawi 2013-14 are requested; they turn region-level blocks into district ones.
- Diet from the household budget surveys for Ghana (GLSS7 food module) and Sierra Leone (SLIHS diary codes), so the 15 diet indicators cover all four countries.
- Conflict events (ACLED, four-country export), market prices for Ghana and Sierra Leone, a decision on FluNet's national counts.
- Every candidate block passes the same test before it enters: within-country sign agreement, paired in-fill with and without it, and leave-one-country-out.

::: {.notes}
The add-on harness is scripts/protocol_v2/39_addon_feature_test.R and it has scored eleven blocks so far; the analysis deck's forest plot of those tests is the record. Most recent blocks moved the index by less than 0.01. The household budget survey block and the MICS block are in the base set for what they add inside a country, where two of the three estimands live; they do not help across borders. The GPS request is with UNICEF; the Ghana and Sierra Leone budget-survey modules are with the research assistant. Cote d'Ivoire, the country we rank with no survey, is missing the 30-year climate normals, which cost 27 of the 101 climate-and-soil columns in its intersection without changing the transport figure; extracting them is a morning's work.
:::

## Predictors recurring across outcomes

```{r importance-patterns}
if (!is.null(IP)) {
  d <- IP |> filter(target == "level", outcomes_in_top20 >= 3) |> arrange(desc(outcomes_in_top20), mean_rank) |> head(12) |>
    transmute(Predictor = column, Domain = domain, `Outcomes (top 20)` = outcomes_in_top20, Signs = signs, `Mean rank` = mean_rank)
  kb(d, digits = 1)
}
```

::: {.notes}
Predictors in the pooled top 20 of three or more of the six outcomes on the level target, with the sign in each. One gradient recurs: districts that are drier and grassier, less productive (lower net and gross primary productivity), more pastoral, poorer (less home ownership, fewer women in paid work, less schooling) and more stunted rank worse on every deficiency. Outcome-specific signals sit below it: hemoglobin C allele frequency and cattle for child iron, the modeled anemia surfaces for women's iron, helminth treatment coverage and the drought index for folate, elevation and coast distance for B12.
:::

## Weighting of the domain components

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="34%"}
Alternative weightings of the same components on the biomarker level. In-country every joint fit loses to the marginal-correlation weights (ridge `r sgn(Q$wsi_ridge)`, elastic net `r sgn(Q$wsi_enet)`, lasso `r sgn(Q$wsi_lasso)`). Across borders the decorrelated index gains `r sgn(Q$ws_decor["d"], 3)` (better in `r Q$ws_decor["b"]` of `r Q$ws_decor["n"]`).
:::
::: {.column width="66%"}
```{r weights, fig.width=5.8, fig.height=5.2, dpi=160}
if (!is.null(WS)) {
  lab <- c(domain_index = "Production index (pooled rank correlation)", index_soft1 = "Soft threshold, |z| < 1 to zero", index_decor = "Decorrelated across domains",
           index_meta = "Replication-weighted (meta z)", ridge_min = "Ridge, inner CV", ridge_nested = "Ridge, nested block CV on rank",
           domain_enet = "Elastic net, inner CV", enet_1se = "Elastic net, one-SE rule", lasso_min = "Lasso, inner CV", sparse20 = "Top 20 predictors, equal weights")
  d <- WS |> filter(target == "level", arm %in% names(lab)) |> cell_ci("spearman", c("estimand", "arm")) |>
    mutate(Model = factor(lab[arm], levels = rev(lab)), Estimand = factor(c(infill = "In-fill", region = "Region", country = "Transport")[estimand], levels = c("In-fill", "Region", "Transport")))
  forest(d, "Model", facet = "Estimand", null = 0, base = 12)
}
```
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
The production weights are the infinite-penalty limit of a ridge regression on the components, so the rows are points along that family plus other sources of evidence for the weights (soft thresholding, meta-analytic replication across training countries, decorrelation across domains). Same folds and outcome-country combinations as every other arm; five in-fill draws. The one-SE rules return the null model in some outcome-country combinations (`r Q$ws_1se_scored` of `r Q$tr_cells` transport outcome-country combinations scored for the elastic net). The twenty-predictor composite gains `r sgn(Q$ws_sparse20["d"], 3)` across borders (better in `r Q$ws_sparse20["b"]` of `r Q$ws_sparse20["n"]`) and costs `r sgn(Q$wsi_sparse20)` in-fill. The soft threshold gained 0.02 across borders on the direct DHS estimates and `r sgn(Q$ws_soft1["d"], 3)` on the smoothed ones, so that gain was a property of noisy inputs. Both gains were found among 21 arms on these outcome-country combinations and are pre-registered for the next country rather than adopted. Prevalence-target version in the appendix.
:::

## Sparse composites

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="34%"}
Equal-weight composites of the top 5, 10 and 20 predictors, membership chosen inside each training fold by back-projected index weight. Twenty predictors cost `r sgn(Q$wsi_sparse20)` in-fill and gain `r sgn(Q$ws_sparse20["d"], 3)` across borders; five predictors cost `r sgn(Q$wsi_sparse5)` in-fill.
:::
::: {.column width="66%"}
```{r sparse, fig.width=5.8, fig.height=4.2, dpi=160}
if (!is.null(WS)) {
  lab <- c(domain_index = "Full index", sparse20 = "Top 20, equal weights", sparse10 = "Top 10, equal weights", sparse10w = "Top 10, index weights", sparse5 = "Top 5, equal weights")
  d <- WS |> filter(target == "level", arm %in% names(lab)) |> cell_ci("spearman", c("estimand", "arm")) |>
    mutate(Model = factor(lab[arm], levels = rev(lab)), Estimand = factor(c(infill = "In-fill", region = "Region", country = "Transport")[estimand], levels = c("In-fill", "Region", "Transport")))
  forest(d, "Model", facet = "Estimand", null = 0, base = 13)
}
```
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
Dawes' improper linear model: direction from the training fold, equal weights, rescaled like the index; nothing is chosen on held-out districts. Weighting the ten by their index weights instead of equally changes nothing. The composite is a transport and communication tool: twenty public layers a ministry can compute. Likely question: which twenty. The next slide lists the child iron members.
:::

## Child iron composite

```{r sparse-members}
if (!is.null(IT) && !is.null(MD)) {
  d <- IT |> filter(outcome == "child_iron", target == "level", rank <= 20) |> arrange(rank) |> left_join(MD[, c("column", "source")], by = "column") |>
    transmute(rank, p = paste0(column, " (", ifelse(beta > 0, "+", "-"), ")"), src = sub(" [(].*$", "", source))
  kb(data.frame(Predictor = d$p[1:10], Source = d$src[1:10], `Predictor ` = d$p[11:20], `Source ` = d$src[11:20], check.names = FALSE), digits = 0)
}
```

::: {.notes}
The twenty columns the four-country fit would deploy for child iron, in order of weight, with the sign of the contribution (plus means more deficiency). `r Q$ci_loco` of the twenty keep their sign in every leave-one-country-out fit and `r Q$ci_rep` in every country's own independent fit. In the benchmark the membership is re-chosen inside each training fold; this is the version fitted on all four countries. The other outcomes' composites are in results/tables/protocol_v2/index_importance_top.csv.
:::

## Urbanicity conditioning

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="34%"}
Transported Spearman of the climate-and-soil index at district level (`r f2(Q$ur_cs)`), the same after partialling out an urbanicity composite (`r f2(Q$ur_partial)`), and urbanicity alone (`r f2(Q$ur_only)`).
:::
::: {.column width="66%"}
```{r urban, fig.width=5.8, fig.height=4.0, dpi=160}
if (!is.null(UR)) {
  d <- UR |> filter(target == "level") |> transmute(tier = ifelse(tier == "admin1", "Regional", "District"), outcome, heldout, `Climate + soil index` = rho_cs, `Partialling out urbanicity` = partial_cs, `Urbanicity alone` = rho_urb_only) |>
    pivot_longer(c(`Climate + soil index`, `Partialling out urbanicity`, `Urbanicity alone`), names_to = "quantity", values_to = "v") |> cell_ci("v", c("tier", "quantity")) |>
    mutate(quantity = factor(quantity, levels = rev(c("Climate + soil index", "Partialling out urbanicity", "Urbanicity alone"))))
  forest(d, "quantity", facet = "tier", null = 0, base = 13)
}
```
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
Urbanicity composite: night lights, population density, built surface, urban land cover, travel time to health care. The replicated associations (legumes, cattle, soil chemistry, night-time temperature, all toward more deficiency) describe where subsistence agriculture is, so an urban-rural gradient was the rival explanation; partialling it out moves the transported correlation by less than 0.02 and urbanicity alone does not transport.
:::

## Add-on predictor blocks

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="34%"}
Median change in Spearman when a block is added to the base vocabulary, in-fill and district transport on the biomarker level, scored under one harness with the same folds.
:::
::: {.column width="66%"}
```{r addons, fig.width=5.8, fig.height=4.8, dpi=160}
tags <- c(food_tm = "Food prices, fieldwork-matched", climate_tm = "Temperature and rainfall, fieldwork-matched", alphaearth = "Satellite embedding as own domain",
          livestock = "Livestock density", water_distance = "Distance to water and coast", espen = "Helminth burden and control", ihme_raster = "IHME surfaces as zonal means",
          fe_clim_aw = "Engineered climatology", fe_terrain_aw = "Terrain", fe_soil_aw = "Soil bioavailability")
rows <- lapply(names(tags), function(t) { i <- rd(P2, paste0("addon_", t, "_infill.csv")); l <- rd(P2, paste0("addon_", t, "_loco.csv")); if (is.null(i) || is.null(l)) return(NULL)
  di <- i |> filter(target == "level") |> group_by(country, outcome) |> summarise(d = mean(spearman[set == "plus"], na.rm = TRUE) - mean(spearman[set == "base"], na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
  dl <- l |> filter(tier == "admin2", target == "level") |> group_by(heldout, outcome) |> summarise(d = mean(spearman[set == "plus"], na.rm = TRUE) - mean(spearman[set == "base"], na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
  bind_rows(df(Block = tags[[t]], Estimand = "In-fill", d = di$d), df(Block = tags[[t]], Estimand = "Transport", d = dl$d)) })
rows <- bind_rows(rows[!sapply(rows, is.null)])
if (nrow(rows)) {
  d <- rows |> group_by(Block, Estimand) |> summarise(est = median(d, na.rm = TRUE), lo = quantile(d, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE), hi = quantile(d, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
  ord <- d |> filter(Estimand == "Transport") |> arrange(est); d$Block <- factor(d$Block, levels = ord$Block)
  ggplot(d, aes(est, Block)) + geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "grey45") + geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), width = 0.25, colour = "grey35", orientation = "y") +
    geom_point(size = 3, colour = "#1f4e79") + facet_wrap(~ Estimand) + labs(x = "Change in Spearman when the block is added (median, IQR over cells)", y = NULL) + theme_minimal(base_size = 12) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
}
```
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
Bars are the interquartile range over outcome-country combinations. No block moves in-fill or transport by more than 0.01 at the median: the vocabulary is saturated. The fieldwork-matched temperature columns are among the most consistently associated with deficiency in the marginal scan yet improve no fold, because a covariate defined by when the survey happened cannot rank districts that have not been surveyed. Found in passing and fixed: the price columns used 2021 as The Gambia's survey year (fieldwork was January to April 2018), and the satellite embedding had been filed under agriculture.
:::

## Cluster-level fitting

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="34%"}
The same index fitted at the survey cluster and aggregated to districts, against the district fit, on the same outcome-country combinations. In-fill on the level: `r f2(Q$cv_agg)` cluster-fitted against `r f2(Q$cv_dist)` district-fitted.
:::
::: {.column width="66%"}
```{r cluster, fig.width=5.8, fig.height=4.2, dpi=160}
if (!is.null(CV)) {
  d <- CV |> filter(set == "transportable", arm == "domain_index") |> transmute(estimand = c(infill = "In-fill", region = "Region")[estimand], target = tlab[target], country, outcome, `Cluster-fitted, aggregated to districts` = rho_agg, `District-fitted` = rho_district_v2) |>
    pivot_longer(c(`Cluster-fitted, aggregated to districts`, `District-fitted`), names_to = "fit", values_to = "v") |> cell_ci("v", c("estimand", "target", "fit")) |>
    mutate(panel = paste(estimand, target, sep = ", "), fit = factor(fit, levels = rev(c("District-fitted", "Cluster-fitted, aggregated to districts"))))
  forest(d, "fit", facet = "panel", null = 0, base = 12)
}
```
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
`r Q$n_clusters` clusters with GPS; covariates as 2 km (urban) and 5 km (rural) buffer means from rasters on disk; the same estimands with folds cut by district and region. Cluster-fitted models trail district-fitted ones on every estimand and for transport. A precision-weighted index and empirical-Bayes shrinkage of cluster outcomes recover a third to a half of the gap. A matched-vocabulary comparison attributes the remaining gap to the layers rather than the fitting unit. The cluster track is a sensitivity analysis until its vocabulary is matched layer for layer.
:::

## Risk-class accuracy

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="34%"}
Share of districts placed in the correct WHO vitamin A band (under 2%, 2 to 10, 10 to 20, 20 or more), and within one band, mean over the vitamin A outcome-country combinations. The index in-fill: `r pc(Q$rc_ex)` exact and `r pc(Q$rc_w1)` within one band.
:::
::: {.column width="66%"}
```{r riskcat, fig.width=5.8, fig.height=4.4, dpi=160}
if (!is.null(RC)) {
  lab <- c(domain_index = "Zero-tuning index, in-fill", spatial_plus_domain = "Smoother + covariates, in-fill", spatial = "Spatial smoother, in-fill", region_mean_jk = "Jackknifed regional mean, in-fill",
           transport_anchored_full = "Transport, full index + national anchor", transport_anchored_climate_soil = "Transport, climate + soil + national anchor")
  d <- RC |> filter(scheme == "who_vitA", arm %in% names(lab)) |> transmute(country, outcome, arm, `Exact band` = exact_admin2, `Within one band` = within1_admin2) |>
    pivot_longer(c(`Exact band`, `Within one band`), names_to = "measure", values_to = "v") |> cell_ci("v", c("arm", "measure")) |> mutate(Model = factor(lab[arm], levels = rev(lab)))
  forest(d, "Model", facet = "measure", null = NA_real_, base = 12, xlab = "Share of districts (mean, 95% interval)") + scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent)
}
```
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
Out-of-fold predictions averaged over ten draws; transport rows use the held-out country's own national prevalence as the anchor (AR-01 design), the only honest way to put a transported ranking on the prevalence scale. The January deck's child vitamin A outcome-country combination was 44 and 75 percent (exact, within one) for the full model from the old leaderboard. For iron and the other outcomes only the 20 percent threshold has a WHO source; the two-class accuracies are in results/tables/protocol_v2/risk_category_accuracy_summary.csv.
:::

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="34%"}
Ghana in-fill on the biomarker level with the base vocabulary, the base plus the LSMS block, and the LSMS block alone, median over ten draws.
:::
::: {.column width="66%"}
```{r lsms, fig.width=5.8, fig.height=4.2, dpi=160}
if (!is.null(LI)) {
  d <- LI |> filter(country == "Ghana", target == "level", set %in% c("base", "plus", "addon_only")) |> group_by(outcome, set) |> summarise(rho = median(spearman, na.rm = TRUE), lo = quantile(spearman, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE), hi = quantile(spearman, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(Outcome = olab[outcome], Set = factor(c(base = "Base vocabulary", plus = "Base + LSMS", addon_only = "LSMS alone")[set], levels = c("Base vocabulary", "Base + LSMS", "LSMS alone")))
  ggplot(d, aes(rho, Outcome, colour = Set)) + geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "grey45") + geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), width = 0.25, orientation = "y", position = position_dodge(width = 0.6)) +
    geom_point(size = 3, position = position_dodge(width = 0.6)) + scale_colour_manual(values = c("Base vocabulary" = "#1f4e79", "Base + LSMS" = "#b15928", "LSMS alone" = "grey50")) +
    labs(x = "Spearman (median, IQR over draws)", y = NULL, colour = NULL) + theme_minimal(base_size = 13) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")

```
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
The LSMS block scored here is Ghana's GLSS7 as a svyby object: 134 region-level household expenditure and asset means, broadcast to districts through the 16-to-10 region crosswalk, so the block varies only across ten regions. It does not improve any Ghana outcome-country combination beyond noise and cannot be scored across borders. The household budget surveys now enter the base set another way, as diet and consumption indicators computed from the microdata for all four countries (GLSS7 for Ghana, again at the region); that block is part of the base vocabulary this slide compares against. FluNet reports for Ghana and Sierra Leone only and is a national weekly count, constant within a country; it contributes nothing by construction.
:::

## Individual-level models

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="34%"}
Person-level SuperLearner under district-blocked folds, Brier skill over the national prevalence, by country and outcome. Mean AUC over `r Q$il_cells` outcome-country combinations: `r f2(Q$il_auc_s)` for survey variables, `r f2(Q$il_auc_p)` for district proxies, `r f2(Q$il_auc_b)` for both.
:::
::: {.column width="66%"}
```{r individual, fig.width=5.8, fig.height=4.6, dpi=160}
if (!is.null(IL) && nrow(IL)) {
  d <- IL |> mutate(Outcome = olab[outcome], set = factor(c(survey_only = "Survey variables only", proxies_only = "District proxies only", both = "Both")[set], levels = c("Survey variables only", "District proxies only", "Both")), country = sub("SierraLeone", "Sierra Leone", country))
  ggplot(d, aes(x = 100 * brier_skill, y = Outcome, colour = set)) + geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") + geom_point(size = 2.6, position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +
    facet_wrap(~ country, nrow = 1) + scale_colour_manual(values = c("Survey variables only" = "#1f4e79", "District proxies only" = "#b15928", "Both" = "grey45")) +
    labs(x = "Brier skill over the national prevalence (%)", y = NULL, colour = NULL) + theme_minimal(base_size = 12) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}
```
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
Library: mean, elastic net, random forest; survey weights; inner folds blocked by district; outer 5-fold by district so no district's respondents are split across training and test. Survey variables: up to 80 respondent columns with 70 percent coverage after removing biomarkers, adjustments, identifiers, weights, dates and locations. Proxies: the district's domain components joined to each respondent. Person-level skill exists for iron only (survey-variable AUC up to `r f2(Q$il_iron_max)` in Ghana and Malawi); vitamin A, folate and B12 show none. The January figure (Brier skill 20 to 60 percent) came from folds not blocked by district and a survey set that included biomarker-adjacent variables. Aggregating a person-level classifier biases area means, so this remains a sensitivity analysis. Rerun on the RR-10 set on 10 September.
:::

## National-level track

```{r national}
if (!is.null(NE)) { d <- NE |> filter(model_type == "binary", outcome %in% c("child_vitA", "women_vitA", "child_iron", "women_iron")) |> group_by(Outcome = olab[outcome]) |>
  summarise(Countries = dplyr::n(), `Observed (mean)` = mean(obs_prev), `Predicted (mean)` = mean(pred_prev), `Mean absolute error (pp)` = 100 * mean(abs_diff), .groups = "drop"); kb(d, digits = 2) }
```

::: {.notes}
The January deck's national-level track (WHO VMNIS and BRINDA outcomes, FAOSTAT and policy predictors) lives in a separate sub-pipeline last run in April 2026. It is not part of the current protocol and has not been re-audited; the table is its last output for the four survey countries. It is the only track with time series and fortification policy indicators and is a candidate for a rerun under the corrected protocol.
:::

## Iodine

```{r iodine}
if (!is.null(IO)) { d <- IO |> filter(analysis == "protocol") |> mutate(cell = paste0(ifelse(country == "Gambia", "Gambia ", "Sierra Leone "), ifelse(target == "p_low", "UIC < 100", "median UIC"), ", ", ifelse(estimand == "infill", "in-fill", "region")),
    Model = c(null_train_mean = "Training mean", region_mean_jk = "Jackknifed regional mean", spatial = "Spatial smoother", domain_index = "Zero-tuning index", spatial_plus_domain = "Smoother + covariates")[arm]) |>
    select(Model, cell, spearman) |> pivot_wider(names_from = cell, values_from = spearman) |> mutate(across(-Model, ~ ifelse(is.finite(.x), sprintf("%.2f", .x), "-"))); kb(d, digits = 2) }
```

::: {.notes}
Urinary iodine is measured in The Gambia (continuous, with household salt iodine) and in Sierra Leone (six WHO categories, non-lactating women); it left the modelling outcomes because a one- or two-country outcome has no leave-one-country-out test. Targets: district prevalence of urinary iodine concentration below 100 micrograms per litre and, for The Gambia, the district median. In-fill needs at least 15 districts, so it runs for The Gambia only; leave-one-region-out runs in both. Whether district salt iodisation tracks district iodine status is in results/tables/protocol_v2/iodine_in_country.csv (rows analysis = descriptive).
:::

## Weighting of the domain components: prevalence

```{r weights-prev, fig.width=10, fig.height=5.0, dpi=140}
if (!is.null(WS)) {
  lab <- c(domain_index = "Production index (pooled rank correlation)", index_soft1 = "Soft threshold, |z| < 1 to zero", index_decor = "Decorrelated across domains",
           index_meta = "Replication-weighted (meta z)", ridge_min = "Ridge, inner CV", ridge_nested = "Ridge, nested block CV on rank",
           domain_enet = "Elastic net, inner CV", enet_1se = "Elastic net, one-SE rule", lasso_min = "Lasso, inner CV", sparse20 = "Top 20 predictors, equal weights")
  d <- WS |> filter(target == "prev", arm %in% names(lab)) |> cell_ci("spearman", c("estimand", "arm")) |>
    mutate(Model = factor(lab[arm], levels = rev(lab)), Estimand = factor(c(infill = "In-fill", region = "Region", country = "Transport")[estimand], levels = c("In-fill", "Region", "Transport")))
  forest(d, "Model", facet = "Estimand", null = 0, base = 13)
}
```

::: {.notes}
Prevalence target, same arms and folds as the biomarker-level figure. Mean Spearman over outcome-country combinations with a 95% interval across outcome-country combinations.
:::

## Geostatistical comparator: absolute error

```{r geostat-wmae, fig.width=10, fig.height=4.6, dpi=140}
if (!is.null(MBG)) {
  lab <- c(domain_index = "Zero-tuning domain index", mbg = "Geostatistical, field + domain covariates", mbg_dhs = "Geostatistical, field + DHS covariate list", mbg_gp = "Geostatistical, field only", spatial = "Spatial smoother", region_mean_jk = "Jackknifed regional mean")
  d <- MBG |> filter(estimand == "infill", target == "prev", arm %in% names(lab)) |> cell_ci("wmae_agg", "arm") |> mutate(Model = factor(lab[arm], levels = rev(lab)))
  forest(d, "Model", null = NA_real_, base = 14, xlab = "Weighted mean absolute error, percentage points (mean, 95% interval)")
}
```

::: {.notes}
In-fill, prevalence. The geostatistical model estimates a level and shrinks uncertain districts toward the mean, which lowers absolute error; the index ranks and is rescaled to the training outcome's spread, which does not. If the deliverable is a prevalence figure for a named district, the geostatistical model is the right tool; if it is a ranking, the index is.
:::

```{r dropped1}
kb(df(`January slide` = c("Individual-level proxy versus survey-only models (Brier skill, AUC, PR gain)", "National-level VMNIS / BRINDA predictions", "Iodine (Sierra Leone)", "Risk-category accuracy (none / mild / moderate / severe)"),
  Status = c("Sensitivity layer; rerun under district-blocked folds", "Separate sub-pipeline, last run April 2026", "Rerun within country (The Gambia, Sierra Leone)", "Rerun under the protocol, WHO bands"),
  Where = c("Individual-level models", "National-level track; not re-audited", "Iodine", "Risk-class accuracy")), digits = 0)
```

::: {.notes}
The individual-level SuperLearner remains a sensitivity analysis because shrinking a noisy individual classifier biases area means; it was removed from the dashboard on 13 September, which now shows only the protocol's index (amertens.shinyapps.io/micronutrient-burden).
:::
